title: viewport/SDFColliderRenderer
summary: SDFColliderRenderer — GPU SDF Raymarcher for COLLISION detection ================================================================ ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW — TWO SEPARATE SDF SYSTEMS: 1. COLLISION SDF (THIS FILE): - Purpose: Physics collision detection via per-pixel GPU raymarching. - How it works: A fullscreen triangle is drawn. For every pixel, the fragment shader raymarches through ALL SDF instances (up to 256) using smooth-min blending (smin) to find the surface. - Cost: EXPENSIVE. O(pixels × instances × marchSteps). At 1080p with 132 capsules and 64 steps, that's ~500M SDF evaluations per frame. - When to use: Only for physics queries that need exact SDF distance fields (e.g. particle-body collision, projectile intersection). - Data flow: Viewport.js (entity loop) → addShape() → instanceBuffer (GPU) → WGSL raymarcher → per-pixel distance field 2. VISUAL OVERLAY (Viewport.js + EntityMeshRenderer): - Purpose: Show a semi-transparent "second skin" over the character mesh so the user can see the collision shape approximation. - How it works: getAnimatedBoneShapes() returns current animated bone positions + mesh-measured capsule sizes. Each bone is rendered as a stretched sphere mesh via EntityMeshRenderer instancing. - Cost: CHEAP. One instanced draw call, standard rasterization. No raymarching, no per-pixel SDF evaluation. - When to use: Always, when the "Show Voxel Colliders" toggle is on. - Data flow: SkeletalAnimation.getAnimatedBoneShapes() → Viewport.js → EntityMeshRenderer.renderEntity() (sphere meshes) RENDERING ORDER (in Viewport.js render loop): 1. Entity meshes (opaque)       — entityMeshRenderer.flush() 2. SDF collision pass            — sdfColliderRenderer.render() [THIS] 3. Rope debug spheres            — entityMeshRenderer (rope particles) 4. Bone visual overlay spheres   — entityMeshRenderer (bone capsules) 5. Bone direction indicators     — boneDirectionLineRenderer 6. Gizmos, grid, ground shadow 7. Post-processing               — bloom, tonemap, reconstruction BLEND MODE: This renderer uses ADDITIVE blending (srcAlpha + one) so the SDF overlay adds color on top of whatever was already rendered. This means: - depthWrite: false (don't occlude other geometry) - depthCompare: 'always' (draw over everything) - The underlying mesh remains visible through the SDF SDF functions are defined in spawnable files and compiled dynamically. Now powered by vGPU driver. Supports: - Primitive shapes (sphere, box, cylinder, capsule, torus) - Custom spawnable shapes (gear, star, helix, etc.) - Universal mesh SDF (auto-fit primitives, triangle sampling, 3D baking)

title: viewport/SkinRenderer
summary: SkinRenderer — System 2: High-Detail Body Skin ================================================ Renders the ACTUAL mesh geometry of the entity, semi-transparent, with a warm skin tone. Full triangle count of the imported model — this is NOT a hull approximation. The mesh IS the skin layer. LAYER ROLE: Inner visible layer — shows the real body geometry as a translucent skin shell. Since it uses the same mesh as the actual entity render, it is perfectly shape-accurate at full detail. VISUAL: - Full-res model mesh, warm skin tone [0.9, 0.6, 0.4, 0.28] - Rendered via the existing 'custom_<uuid>' mesh key already in EntityMeshRenderer - No separate mesh registration needed — the mesh is already uploaded DATA SOURCE: EntityMeshRenderer already has the 'custom_<uuid>' mesh registered when the entity loads. No separate computation needed — just pass entity transform directly. INDEPENDENCE: - No external imports needed beyond EntityMeshRenderer (draw) - No reference to AuraRenderer, SkeletonRenderer, SDFColliderRenderer

title: workers/CollabSignalWorker
summary: CollabSignalWorker.js — SharedWorker In-memory SDP relay for all editor tabs on the same machine. Runs once per origin, shared across all tabs. Message types (client → worker): HELLO    { peerId, username } OFFER    { from, to, offerId, payload } ANSWER   { from, to, offerId, payload } CANDIDATE { from, to, offerId, payload } LEAVE    { peerId } LIST     (request peer list) Message types (worker → client): HELLO_ACK   { peerId, peers: [{peerId, username}] } PEER_JOINED { peerId, username } PEER_LEFT   { peerId } OFFER       { from, to, offerId, payload } ANSWER      { from, to, offerId, payload } CANDIDATE   { from, to, offerId, payload } LIST        { peers: [{peerId, username}] }
